title: Step 4: player clicked 'Play Unit — Petal Pixie to base' with 2 energy available (cost 2). In the AFTER state/screenshot nothing about the play is reflected: Petal Pixie still in hand, base empty, energy still 2, no toast/rejection, no in-flight indicator. The only visible change is the tail of the PREVIOUS action (quickRecycleRune's deferred recycle of the Order Rune landing: rune gone, +1 Order,
expected: Trace verified: step 03→04→05 shows exactly the described one-step lag (04: energy 2, power.order 0→1, runePool 2→1, base [], Pixie still in hand; 05: base=[Petal Pixie], energy 0, hand 9→8). Screenshot mtimes (03=33.565s, 04=34.095s, 05=34.625s) with the harness's fixed `waitForTimeout(400)` (monkey-drive.ts:280) mean the playUnit round-trip exceeded ~400ms on localhost. Source confirms both halves of the mechanism: (1) UI: the action-panel Play Unit button calls executeMove directly (render/actions.js:341-342), and executeMove is pure fire-and-forget `ws.send({type:"move"...})` with no pending state, button disable, or optimistic render (game-flow.js:25-26); the only in-flight guard, `window.__rbTurnActionInFlight`, is a non-visual space/end-turn double-press latch (init.js:31-40, hotkeys.js:266-268) and is not set for panel plays. (2) Server: gameWsMessage runs executeMove → buildGameSnapshot → buildAvailableMoves(actor) synchronously before ws.send(move_accepted) (server/ws-game.ts:90-161), then keeps blocking the single event loop with buildAvailableMoves+snapshot per other client (163-178) and sandbox goldfish auto-play (181+), so the next queued move (Pixie) cannot start until the prior recycleRune's tail work finishes. Step 03's 'Order Rune (ready)' indeed routes through quickRecycleRune (render/actions.js:366-368 → interactions.js:427-455, deferred recycle via 100ms setTimeout poll), matching the 'tail of previous action' description. Minor nit: actor reply is sent before other-seat enumeration, not after, but the effective latency claim holds because of event-loop serialization. Low-severity responsiveness/feedback finding, not a rules violation, as the claim itself states.
